questions.stem:
$\frac{9x^2}{(x-1)^2(2x+1)} = \frac{A}{(x-1)}+\frac{B}{(x-1)^2}+\frac{C}{(2x+1)}$

Find the values of the constants $A$, $B$ and $C$.
(4)

parts.text:
$\frac{9x^2}{(x-1)^2(2x+1)} = \frac{A}{(x-1)}+\frac{B}{(x-1)^2}+\frac{C}{(2x+1)}$

Find the values of the constants $A$, $B$ and $C$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: $9x^2 = A(x-1)(2x+1)+B(2x+1)+C(x-1)^2$
M1: $x\to 1$: $9=3B \Rightarrow B=3$
A1: (Any two of $A$, $B$, $C$) $x\to -\frac{1}{2}$: $\frac{9}{4}=\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 C \Rightarrow C=1$
A1: (All three correct) $x^2$ terms: $9=2A+C \Rightarrow A=4$
Alternatives for finding $A$: $x$ terms $0=-A+2B-2C \Rightarrow A=4$; Constant terms $0=-A+B+C \Rightarrow A=4$

questions.stem:
$\mathrm{f}(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{(9+4x^2)}}$, $|x|<\frac{3}{2}$

Find the first three non-zero terms of the binomial expansion of $\mathrm{f}(x)$ in ascending powers of $x$. Give each coefficient as a simplified fraction.
(6)

parts.text:
$\mathrm{f}(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{(9+4x^2)}}$, $|x|<\frac{3}{2}$

Find the first three non-zero terms of the binomial expansion of $\mathrm{f}(x)$ in ascending powers of $x$. Give each coefficient as a simplified fraction.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $\mathrm{f}(x)=(\ldots+\ldots)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$
B1: $=9^{-\frac{1}{2}}(\ldots+\ldots)^{\ldots}$ ($3^{-1}$, $\frac{1}{3}$ or $\frac{1}{9^{\frac{1}{2}}}$)
M1: $(1+kx^2)^n = 1+nkx^2+\ldots$ ($n$ not a natural number, $k\neq 1$)
A1 ft: $(1+kx^2)^{-\frac{1}{2}} = \ldots+\frac{(-\frac{1}{2})(-\frac{3}{2})}{2}(kx^2)^2$ (ft their $k\neq 1$)
A1: $\left(1+\frac{4}{9}x^2\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}} = 1-\frac{2}{9}x^2+\frac{2}{27}x^4$
A1: $\mathrm{f}(x)=\frac{1}{3}-\frac{2}{27}x^2+\frac{2}{81}x^4$

questions.stem:
Figure 1

A hollow hemispherical bowl is shown in Figure 1. Water is flowing into the bowl. When the depth of the water is $h$ m, the volume $V\mathrm{m}^3$ is given by

$V = \frac{1}{12}\pi h^2(3-4h)$, $0 \leqslant h \leqslant 0.25$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1: $\frac{dV}{dh}=\frac{1}{2}\pi h-\pi h^2$ (or equivalent)
M1 A1: At $h=0.1$, $\frac{dV}{dh}=\frac{1}{2}\pi(0.1)-\pi(0.1)^2=0.04\pi$ ($\frac{\pi}{25}$)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Water flows into the bowl at a rate of $\frac{\pi}{800}\,\mathrm{m}^3\mathrm{s}^{-1}$.

(b) Find the rate of change of $h$, in $\mathrm{m\,s}^{-1}$, when $h=0.1$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $\frac{dh}{dt}=\frac{dV}{dt}\div\frac{dV}{dh}=\frac{\pi}{800}\times\frac{1}{\frac{1}{2}\pi h-\pi h^2}$ (or $\frac{\pi}{800}\div$ their (a))
A1: At $h=0.1$, $\frac{dh}{dt}=\frac{\pi}{800}\times\frac{25}{\pi}=\frac{1}{32}$ (awrt 0.031)

questions.stem:
Figure 2

Figure 2 shows a sketch of the curve with equation $y=x^3\ln(x^2+2)$, $x\geqslant 0$.
The finite region $R$, shown shaded in Figure 2, is bounded by the curve, the $x$-axis and the line $x=\sqrt{2}$.

The table below shows corresponding values of $x$ and $y$ for $y=x^3\ln(x^2+2)$.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 0 & \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} & \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4} & \sqrt{2}\\ \hline y & 0 & & 0.3240 & & 3.9210\\ \hline\end{array}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Complete the table above giving the missing values of $y$ to 4 decimal places.
(2)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Use the trapezium rule, with all the values of $y$ in the completed table, to obtain an estimate for the area of $R$, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.
(3)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Use the substitution $u=x^2+2$ to show that the area of $R$ is

$\frac{1}{2}\int_{2}^{4}(u-2)\ln u\,du$
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: $u=x^2+2 \Rightarrow \frac{du}{dx}=2x$
B1: Area($R$) $=\int_{0}^{\sqrt{2}} x^3\ln(x^2+2)\,dx$
M1: $\int x^3\ln(x^2+2)\,dx = \int x^2\ln(x^2+2)\,x\,dx = \int(u-2)(\ln u)\frac{1}{2}\,du$
A1 cso: Hence Area($R$) $=\frac{1}{2}\int_{2}^{4}(u-2)\ln u\,du$ *

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Hence, or otherwise, find the exact area of $R$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1 A1: $\int(u-2)\ln u\,du = \left(\frac{u^2}{2}-2u\right)\ln u - \int\left(\frac{u^2}{2}-2u\right)\frac{1}{u}\,du$
M1 A1: $=\left(\frac{u^2}{2}-2u\right)\ln u - \int\left(\frac{u}{2}-2\right)du = \left(\frac{u^2}{2}-2u\right)\ln u - \left(\frac{u^2}{4}-2u\right)(+C)$
M1: Area($R$) $=\frac{1}{2}\left[\left(\frac{u^2}{2}-2u\right)\ln u - \left(\frac{u^2}{4}-2u\right)\right]_2^4 = \frac{1}{2}\left[(8-8)\ln 4-4+8-((2-4)\ln 2-1+4)\right]$
A1: $=\frac{1}{2}(2\ln 2+1)$ ($\ln 2+\frac{1}{2}$)

M1: $\approx \ldots[0+2(0.0333+0.3240+1.3596)+3.9210]$
A1: $\approx 1.30$ (Accept 1.3)
B1: $u=x^2+2 \Rightarrow \frac{du}{dx}=2x$

A1: $=\frac{1}{2}(2\ln 2+1)$ ($\ln 2+\frac{1}{2}$)

questions.stem:
Find the gradient of the curve with equation

$\ln y = 2x\ln x$, $x>0$, $y>0$

at the point on the curve where $x=2$. Give your answer as an exact value.
(7)

parts.text:
Find the gradient of the curve with equation

$\ln y = 2x\ln x$, $x>0$, $y>0$

at the point on the curve where $x=2$. Give your answer as an exact value.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: $\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}=\ldots$
M1 A1: $\ldots = 2\ln x+2x\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)$
M1: At $x=2$, $\ln y=2(2)\ln 2$
A1: leading to $y=16$ (Accept $y=e^{4\ln 2}$)
M1: At $(2,16)$, $\frac{1}{16}\frac{dy}{dx}=2\ln 2+2$
A1: $\frac{dy}{dx}=16(2+2\ln 2)$
Alternative: B1: $y=e^{2x\ln x}$; M1 A1: $\frac{d}{dx}(2x\ln x)=2\ln x+2x\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)$; M1 A1: $\frac{dy}{dx}=\left(2\ln x+2x\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\right)e^{2x\ln x}$; M1: At $x=2$, $\frac{dy}{dx}=(2\ln 2+2)e^{4\ln 2}$; A1: $=16(2+2\ln 2)$
